missing: Nobody compares both routes side by side for full-time use: expandable power stations (about 1–8 kWh) and full 48V kits (10 kWh and up). That means no clear verdict on which kits can really cover a 6–10 kWh day through winter, no current prices across brands, and no checked discount codes.
why: No major reviewer or authority shows up. The results are two Renogy pages, a New Zealand brand page, a store's own buying guide, one niche spec comparison that says it did no testing, an affiliate listicle, an off-target balcony-solar page and five pages with no text. A focused page could stand out by comparing kits for a full-time tiny house or cabin on daily kWh, winter solar input, expansion and current price.
